notes:
DOMAIN SUBSTITUTION (Rule 3): the assigned roster domain hk-living.com is a dead/parked domain, not the real HKliving site. DNS resolves it to a single IPv4-only host (95.211.13.71, no AAAA record) that direct-connect and curl (-4/-6) both fail to reach (connect timeout, confirmed IPv4 egress dead to this specific host across multiple attempts). translate.goog could reach only /robots.txt (200, 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /' -- a blanket disallow-all, not Claude-specific) but 404'd 'Can't reach this website' on the homepage. Wayback CDX history for hk-living.com shows its last real 200 content was 2019-07-28 and is a LeaseWeb 'this domain has been registered by a LeaseWeb customer' parking placeholder (~2.3KB), unchanged back to at least 2011 -- this domain has never hosted the actual HKliving catalogue. The genuine, live, actively-maintained HKliving brand site is hkliving.com (no dash; confirmed via web search as 'the official HKliving website', Cloudflare-fronted, live Umbraco/VWA CMS site, title 'HKLIVING: Creating ambience'). Extracted from https://www.hkliving.com/ per Rule 3 ('if it redirects to a different live catalogue, extract that and say so -- your links won't match the roster domain, which is fine when documented'); this is not a literal redirect but the same real-world Dutch brand at its actual working domain. robots.txt on hkliving.com (the domain actually used) 404s -- no robots.txt file exists there, so no Claude-specific or blanket disallow applies to the site actually extracted. SITE NATURE: hkliving.com is a B2B/wholesale-facing trade catalogue (nav: 'Become a dealer', 'Agents & Distributors', 'Where can I buy HKLIVING?' -> store locator; no visible prices/checkout) rather than a direct consumer webshop -- matches the brief's boutique/designer-brand note. Product browsing and category counts are fully public with no login/dealer-account wall encountered. ACCESS METHOD: category pages render their product grid client-side via an Umbraco AJAX endpoint, /umbraco/surface/AsyncContentSurface/Index (POST, JSON), driven by a categoryId read from each page's hidden #__CategoryId input plus a per-session CSRF RequestVerificationToken (cookie + hidden-field pair). Direct static HTML fetch shows only 'Loading filter please wait...' with no counts; replaying the real AJAX call (session cookies + token + categoryId, doGroupProducts=1 matching the page's own default) returns JSON whose articlelist_container HTML includes a 'N' -- the exact number the site itself renders next to the 'Filter products' button for a real visitor. All qty values below are this totalcount field. VERIFICATION (Rule 1): counting rendered
tiles/hrefs was explicitly NOT used as primary evidence -- confirmed unreliable here exactly as the project has seen elsewhere: Mirrors showed 15 grouped swatch-cards for totalcount=16 because one card bundles 2 distinct colour SKUs (dressing-table-mirror-petrol + -candy) under one swatch selector (15 cards - 1 + 2 = 16, reconciles exactly); Pendant Lamps showed 16 tiles on page 1 for totalcount=17, and page 2 (PageIndex=1) returned exactly 1 further article, confirming full pagination exhaustion (16+1=17). Where a category fit on one page, the pager's forward-button disabled state confirmed no further pages existed. EXCLUDED (whole company): Sofas, Furniture (benches/cabinets & shelves/dining chairs/dining tables/fauteuils/side tables/stools), Textile (bath mats/bed linen/cushions/rugs/wall rugs/towels & robes) -- furniture/textile. Outdoor furniture, Outdoor textile -- furniture/textile. Outdoor accessories (4 items: 3 patio umbrellas [furniture/shade equipment] + 1 terracotta floor vase AFC0007) -- dropped whole node: predominantly non-decor, and its sole decor item is already counted under the main Vases category (confirmed via SKU-set check, AFC0007 present in Vases, absent from Flowerpots). Cutlery, Table linen -- flatware/textile. Home fragrances (19 items: fragrance sticks, scented candles) -- Home Fragrance rule. Clothing racks (1 item) -- furniture. Lookbooks (3 items) -- printed marketing publications, not products. Tableware (370 SKUs) -- dropped as a mixed roll-up: full-SKU-set comparison showed 353/370 (95%) already contained in the union of the kept sibling type categories (Mugs & Cups, Plates, Bowls, Glassware, Kitchen Accessories, Serveware & Display) plus the ceramics lines; Chef/Artist/Shell ceramics are 100% subsets of it and 70s Ceramics is 87% contained -- Tableware is essentially 'Kitchen minus a few outliers', not a distinct type. Art (80 items) -- dropped as a redundant cross-cut: 71/78 SKUs (91%) already counted under Wall Decoration (82% of Wall Decoration's own SKUs recur here), Objects & Sculptures, Vases and Candle Holders. 'Brand kit' and 'Add ons' product-nav pages -- no categoryId / no article-list component found, not real product-listing categories. Collections / Catalogues / Collaborations nav (Additions 2026, Collection 25-26, Fresh stock, etc.) -- marketing/collection pages per the NEVER EXTRACT rule. RULE 0 / 0.6: no room-based lighting split exists on this site (checked -- no 'Lighting by Room', no bathroom/vanity/outdoor lighting nodes at all, so Rule 0.1 had nothing to gain here); Outdoor was not blanket-excluded for its room word -- its one eligible decor item was individually traced and found already captured under Vases before dropping the node. The four ceramics-line categories (70s Ceramics, Chef Ceramics, Artist Ceramics, Shell Ceramics) are a genuine second navigational dimension of Kitchen (the site's own material/collection-line tree) that cross-tags heavily into the product-type tree (87% of Mugs & Cups, 60% of Bowls, 54% of Plates fall inside 70s Ceramics) -- both trees are kept per Rule 0.6 since each is a real distinct site nav node with its own URL and total, not a pure filter re-cut; overlap documented here rather than dropping either side. Kitchen Accessories and Serveware & Display similarly show partial (~55-70%) mutual overlap and modest (~21-38%) overlap with Bowls -- kept for the same reason. CURRENCY: no prices are shown pre-login (trade catalogue), so EUR was not directly observed, but is expected for a Dutch brand; not itself evidence of a different catalogue.
